title: Spanish Indie Music
content: Ok, here we go with something i like, something i discovered when i was living in Spain, “la escena musical indie española”. I knew some Spanish music, but when i moved to Spain and i started to listen Cariño, my mind was blown. I started to listen more and more Spanish music from the same production company, Elefant Records. I remember that was the COVID time, and the first time i could see Cariño live was in small presentation in Aranjuez (a small city near Madrid). I started to follow more and more Spanish indie music, particuarly at that time i'd say that was the bum of the Spanish indie music. Cariño, Ginebras, Axolotes Mexicanos, between others, were just at the bum of their career. I know, there were some other bands before, like Papa Topo or La Casa Azul (the ones who started Elefant Records), but i think many bands started to be more popular at that time. Still know there're many other bands and artist, Las Dianas, Russian Red or Lisa Sinson, Pipiolas, Aiko el Grupo, Jordana B, Camera Obscura, Marlena, Cola Jet Set, just to name a few. It's quite ineresting to see how the Spanish music is evolving and how the lyrics change, from the first steps of the Spanish (pop/indie/ne) music with Los Bravos and Fórmula V to this new era, but what can i add?, ig there's no better analysis for that times than the one given by Victor from Music Radar Clan in this video.

title: Early Years
content:
My childhood was pretty much the stereotypical introvert childhood: a
passion for things like astronomy, barely speaking to anyone unless an
adult said it was mandatory, never really understanding social interaction.
What else can i say about my first 12 or 13 years of life?, in reality, no
one really makes decisions below that age. Some might argue that even
throughout our entire lives we're completely conditioned by our
environment, but at least during secondary school or high school we start
to make decisions: what degree to choose, what hobbies to pursue, who to
date, what music to listen to, what clothes to wear.

That's when i started thinking about what i would do. I started playing the
guitar when i was 13 yo and i started liking music outside of what my parents
listened to, and i started thinking seriously about life —a bit philosophical
for a teenager, i guess—. but when people ask me “how did you do
something?”, the answer is usually: no friends and a lot of free time. And
with that two things you can start to do many things… including getting
crazy.

At the end of high school comes the moment where you say, “ok, maybe i'll
choose something i'll do for the rest of my life”. i still think that if
i'd had a really good physics course, i might have become a physicist
instead of a chemist, but what's done is done —and i like chemistry, don't
get me wrong, they two aren't opposites—. I also considered studying
philosophy, and sometimes i still wonder what my life would have been
like if i hadn't taken the science path.

title: My Setup
content: Nothing fancy but in case you wanna know what i use, here you have, my setup: MacBook Air M1, iPad Air 2022, iPhone 14 Pro. Yes, an Apple fangirl, i also had an Apple Watch but i didn't like it, now it's in a drawer… and not because i found a better option for a smart watch, but because i think an analogy watch is better. If you were thinking if i had another macBook before, yes i used to use the macBook Pro at the time of intel, about iPhones… 3Gs, 5s, 6s, SE 2020 and 14 Pro. I'm not a apple fanboy, their products are just ok for me, i don't care about the brand. i have my dotfiles in a GitHub repository, it's not the most fancy thing ever but i consider that for me it's enough, i like to keep the things easy, i usually use my computer just with the terminal and the web browser, the only game i ever installed is Minecraft. I use GIMP, Blender and Inkscape for pixel images, 3D render/animation and vector images, LaTeX for writing, Keynote for presentation and manim for some math animations. For my Rouen flat i have an AT-LP60xBT connected by RCA to Edifier R1700BT speakers. At my parents home i have an AT-LP120x with another pair of Edifier but the R1280DB, i also connect by optical audio cable a PS3 because they can read CD and SuperAudio CD. i play the guitar, sadly thre of my guitars are at my parents home, a Fender CD-60S is always waiting my when i go to Mexico, but it's ok, in Europe i have an Epiphone Casino and a Höfner 500/1 Violin Bass. My pedalboar is simple: Vox wah-wah V845, Digitech Whammy V, Boss distortion pedal DS-2, Boss Chorus Ensemble CE-5 and a Boss Digital Delay DD-7. I also play the keyboard and the harmonic.

title: Studies
content: During my bachelor's degree, not much happened. I was just someone who followed the book —what everyone imagines a chemistry student to be, nothing more—. Ok, one hobby (music), et pas plus. not a video-game friki, not a language nerd, not a chess player, and definitely not a popular kid. Academically, there were a few turning points. Maybe the first was electromagnetism, i failed it, during kinematics and dynamics i was just solving problems without really understanding them —just another mandatory course—. Electromagnetism was different. when i had to properly study to pass the exam, i don't know how, but i ended up getting 10/10, and i started to like physics. The second turning point was quantum mechanics, again, i initially thought “another mandatory course”, but i loved it. from that moment on, i knew i wanted to be a theoretical chemist. During the last part of my bachelor's degree (five years in mexico), i started taking astrophysics classes. I still love astro-things (astrocositas). By then, i knew i wanted to do a master's degree, so i applied to astrophysics in Australia and to theoretical chemistry in Spain (TCCM —an amazing master if you like theoretical chemistry—). I wasn't sure what to choose, but the decision wasn't entirely mine —it was in the hands? of covid—, the pandemic decided for me: i moved to Spain. A completely new chapter started: postgraduate life. Maybe not the best financial decision, but definitely a fun one. During the second year of my master's, i did an erasmus in Paris, it was a really nice time, and i decided i wanted to stay longer in France —not Paris, but Rouen—. I decided to do a PhD, because… why not? phd time. And apparently not satisfied with avoiding a “real” job, i decided to do a postdoc.
